grep.name: search_repository
grep.description: Find where something appears in the service's source. Answers with every matching line as 'path:line: text'. START HERE: the investigation has already named the cause, so search for it - the flag, the function, the message from the log line - and the answer tells you which files to read. Plain text, not a regular expression.

query.description: The text to look for. Something distinctive from the cause - a flag name, a function name, an error message.

grep.name: list_repository_files
grep.description: List every file in the service's repository, as paths from its root. A fallback for when searching found nothing and you need to see the shape of the repository - prefer a search, which tells you which file to open rather than leaving you to guess from names. A repository that could not be listed whole is reported as a failure, never as a shorter list.

grep.name: read_repository_file
grep.description: Read one file's entire contents. Call it several times in the same turn when you want several files - every result comes back together, and a turn spent on one file re-sends everything you have read so far. Read a file before you rewrite it - what you submit replaces what is there, so a file you did not read is a file you are overwriting blind.

path.description: The file's path from the repository root.

meaning.name: search_repository_by_meaning
meaning.description: Find code by describing what it does, when you have no exact text to search for. Answers with passages of the service's source - each one 'path:start-end' and the lines themselves - nearest in meaning to your description. Use this where searching for exact text cannot help: the investigation described a behaviour ('the discount is divided by a count that can be zero') and the repository may not contain any of those words. Describe the behaviour and the mistake, not an identifier. Where you can also search for exact text, do both rather than one instead of the other - one matches characters, this matches meaning.

description.description: What the code you are looking for does, in a sentence - the behaviour and what is wrong with it, as you would describe it to another engineer.
